piece_title: The Morrowind screens, round 6 — the container's gold column and its clipped description

critic.note: I was handed the builder's status file as my work list by the brief, so I read it BEFORE measuring — a deviation from CRITIC-DOCTRINE §8's ordering, recorded here rather than hidden. It cuts one way only: the builder's central claim is the thing I set out to falsify, and I falsified it.

headline: Round 6 fixed both defects it was sent to fix, and introduced a hard fail doing it. The gold column now draws on all seven rows and the description now ellipsises instead of vanishing — both verified from my own captures. But the same change drops the container's RI-UIX09 D2 from 0.1538 to 0.1459, across DN4's 0.15 hard-fail floor, and the builder's claim that it moves D2 by 0.0000 came from a four-arm experiment in which no arm ran the code it named. Round 5's numbers reproduce exactly at round 5's own pin.

job_1_the_reproduction_question.ruling: ROUND 5'S FILED NUMBERS ARE CORRECT AND THEY REPRODUCE EXACTLY. TODAY'S NUMBERS ARE ALSO CORRECT. THE INSTRUMENT IS DETERMINISTIC. The builder's four arms are void — none of them ran the tree it named.
job_1_the_reproduction_question.how_the_arms_were_void: tools/lib/cli.mjs:11 derives REPO_ROOT from the SCRIPT'S OWN location, and tools/lib/browser.mjs resolveEntry() (line 81/91) serves REPO_ROOT/game. So an arm is isolated only if it is run through the CLONE'S OWN copy of the tool. t4-r2-measure.mjs:296 records `git rev-parse HEAD` with cwd=REPO_ROOT. All four of the builder's manifests record a LIVE SIBLING's HEAD, timestamped to the minute each arm ran: 22d6fb39 (17:15, a gitignore commit), f42cb9be (17:24, F10 r9), 0a67808f (17:39, F10 r9 status), dffbd4bc (17:44, F10 r9 critic). None is HEAD, none is the pin.
proof_that_a_real_arm_records_differentl: A control clone built with tools/control-clone.mjs resolves REPO_ROOT to /tmp/elder-souls-control-clones/... where `git rev-parse HEAD` THROWS, so the tool records commit:"unknown". Measured, this run.
A real `git worktree add --detach <dir> 76cd4848` resolves REPO_ROOT to the worktree and records commit:76cd4848... Measured, this run.

Therefore arm 4 — claimed to be a byte-identical worktree at 76cd4848 — recorded a sibling's SHA because it ran the SHARED tree's tools, and so served the SHARED tree's game/. The same holds for arms 1-3.

job_1_the_reproduction_question.is_the_instrument_non_deterministic: NO. I recomputed d2() over round 5's OWN stored PNGs and got 0.1522 / 0.1538 / 0.1449 back exactly, and over round 6's stored PNGs got 0.1495 / 0.1459 exactly. Same image in, same number out. The variance the builder saw was never in the measure; it was that every arm rendered the same tree.

but_the_measure_IS_fragile_and_here_is_t.finding: D2 re-derives its own reference (the panel's modal colour) per capture, and a large pixel population sits at the dE=6 boundary. On the container panel, 0.67% of the panel lies in the dE 5.5-6.5 band, and sweeping the threshold 5.0 -> 7.0 moves D2 from 0.1756 to 0.1599 at the pin and 0.1678 to 0.1523 at HEAD — a span of ~0.0157, roughly FOUR TIMES round 5's entire 0.0038 margin over the hard-fail floor.
but_the_measure_IS_fragile_and_here_is_t.the_sharper_case: The sheet panel differs between the two captures by 166 pixels (0.06% of the panel) and its MODAL COLOUR moved [42,55,43] -> [45,57,45] — and D2 moved 0.0108. Level-up differs by 66 pixels (0.03%), modal colour moved [221,220,211] -> [220,217,204], D2 moved 0.0026. A sub-perceptual shift in the panel's ground re-scores every pixel in the panel against a new reference.
but_the_measure_IS_fragile_and_here_is_t.consequence_for_RI_UIX09: DN4's 0.15 floor is being applied to a quantity whose sensitivity to imperceptible input change exceeds the margins it is adjudicating. That is a finding about the ROW, not about any build, and it is the third member of the family S58 and S59 name. It is filed as a corpus defect below, NOT used to excuse this round.
but_the_measure_IS_fragile_and_here_is_t.why_this_does_not_rescue_the_container: The container's fall is consistent at EVERY threshold (0.1756->0.1678 at dE5.0, 0.1657->0.1572 at dE6.0, 0.1599->0.1523 at dE7.0) and its modal colour did NOT move. It is real matter loss, not threshold drift — and the delete-the-fix arm below attributes it.

job_3_the_declared_cost_judged.the_scoping_claim_is_TRUE_but_the_citati: The builder cites 'T4-r5.md line 773' in writing. corpus/90-verdicts/wave1/T4-r5.md is 472 lines long; there is no line 773. The intended source is T4-r5.JSON line 773, and T4-r5.md line 137 says the same thing. The substance is verified independently: RI-UIX09 P3 reads 'the HUD's quick-slot cluster' and DN3's row is 'P3 quick slots'. DN3 IS scoped to the quick-slot cluster and does not fail a container list row. The claim is right; the citation is a file-name error and is recorded because a citation that resolves to nothing is how a number survives unchecked.
job_3_the_declared_cost_judged.so_is_the_truncation_acceptable: NO — and it does not need a judgement call, because an existing row already settles half of it and a measurement settles the other half.
job_3_the_declared_cost_judged.half_one_the_description_RI_UIX03_C7: RI-UIX03 C7: 'selecting an item shows: name, weight, value, condition/durability if applicable, and the full `description` string, unabbreviated and untruncated'. C8 puts containers on that same screen ('corpses, chests and barrels use the same screen'). The shipped band shows 2 of 4-6 lines ending in an ellipsis, for 42 of 45 carried records. C7 is violated. C7 is judged by M-C3, which requires ALL FOUR of C6/C7/C8/C9, so M-C3 now fails. Round 5's remedy offered 'equals the declared string, OR ends in an ellipsis' — a verdict's remedy cannot licence what a reference item forbids, and CRITIC-DOCTRINE §1.3 guard 1 forbids me relaxing C7 to accept it. The builder followed the remedy in good faith; the remedy was under-specified against C7.
job_3_the_declared_cost_judged.half_two_the_columns_and_a_defect_the_bu: The builder reported the NAME column's cost. It did not report that the same 27% cut truncates the WEIGHT column: 'Bog-iron maul 11.5' becomes 'Bog-iron ... 11...' — a NUMERIC VALUE rendered unreadable. Visible in my own two-arm crop pair. A truncated name is an inconvenience; a weight shown as '11...' is a number the player cannot use to decide what to leave behind, which is precisely the decision RI-UIX03 C6 says value-per-weight exists to serve.
job_3_the_declared_cost_judged.and_it_is_measurable: The truncation is not only a look. It is the matter loss that the delete-the-fix arm attributes: seven rows lost glyphs from the name and weight columns and gained six short gold figures, net -0.0079 on D2, across DN4's floor.
job_3_the_declared_cost_judged.on_growing_the_box_the_builder_s_reasoni: The builder declined to grow the box, citing S58's corrected mechanism (a bigger box without proportionally more ink lowers D2). That reasoning is correct as far as it goes and the restraint was right. But the real reason it was right is sharper: the delete-the-fix arm shows the container had only 0.0038 of headroom and this round spent 0.0079 of it, so ANY change to that screen that is not ink-positive now fails DN4. The remedy is not to grow the box and it is not to revert — it is that the row is too narrow for what it carries, which is S56's shrink-the-box question arriving from the other side, exactly as the brief anticipated.

the_unsatisfiable_clause.the_builder_s_derivation_is_CONFIRMED_by: game/src/ui/screens/progress.js (byte-unchanged across 76cd4848..b0a9f716): the sheet's attribute row declares rect [ax, y, attrW, (attrH-4)*s] and inside it draws the gauge trough at gx = r[0]+40*s, gw = r[2]-56*s, gy = r[1]+26*s — i.e. from x+40 to x+(attrW-16), spanning nearly the row's full width, on its own line BELOW the name/value text, on every row. tools/ui/t4-r4-critic-overlap.mjs's rowProfile() marks a column 'ink' if ANY pixel across the row's FULL height differs from the modal colour. The gauge therefore paints nearly every column, no run of >=3 empty columns can exist, and `rows_with_fewer_than_two_separators: 0` is unsatisfiable on the sheet regardless of legibility. Level-up draws name, value and gauge side by side on ONE line, so its half of the clause tests what it was written to test and is unaffected. CONFIRMED.
the_unsatisfiable_clause.the_proposed_replacement_is_JUDGED_CORRE: Restricting the sheet's arm to the text sub-band — rowProfile() against [ax, y, attrW, 20*s], the name/value line, ending before the gauge starts at y+26*s — measures the thing round 4's remedy meant (does the name collide with the value) without asking a two-line row to behave like a one-line row. It is the right fix.
the_unsatisfiable_clause.I_DID_NOT_LAND_IT_AND_HERE_IS_WHY: CRITIC-DOCTRINE §1.3 guard 1 lets a critic ADD but never relax; guard 3 says bound it. The clause currently fails closed, and rewriting it makes it satisfiable — i.e. it could become the reason a piece passes. I am the critic scoring this piece, so landing it mid-round would be grading against an instrument I had just loosened, which is the same conflict that kept the round-5 critic off RI-UIX06 and this builder off this file. Filed as owed, with the exact patch specified above so it costs the next agent nothing. REVERSIBLE: the orchestrator may land it directly — it bears on no score in this verdict, because I scored the sheet arm fail-closed exactly as it stands.
the_unsatisfiable_clause.who_owns_it: The orchestrator or the next T4 builder. It is a two-line change to tools/ui/t4-r4-critic-overlap.mjs.

the_ui_metrics_question_the_brief_asked_.state: tools/metrics/ui-metrics.mjs exists and runs (38,647 bytes). Its screen list is `const SCREENS = String(args.screens || 'inventory,journal,book,levelup,sheet,spells,map').split(',')` at line 63. The container is NOT in it. The builder's statement is accurate.
the_ui_metrics_question_the_brief_asked_.why_it_is_not_a_one_word_fix: The run loop at line 378 opens each screen with `h.h('openMenu', screen)`. A container does not open that way — system.js opens it via openContainer(name, contents) with an entity, which is why every container-capable instrument in tools/ui/ has its own opener. Adding 'container' to the default list would open nothing and measure nothing.
the_ui_metrics_question_the_brief_asked_.whose_job: NOT the next T4 builder's, and not a critique's to build (§1.3 guard 3). It is a HARNESS gap and belongs to whoever owns tools/metrics/ui-metrics.mjs: give its loop a container branch mirroring t4-r2-measure.mjs's `HH.openContainer(...)` call, then FD1/FD2/FD3/FD5/FD6/FD7 become reachable on the container for the first time. Until then those six checks are unmeasured ON THE CONTAINER and I have scored them 0 fail-closed per §7.3, which is part of why RI-UIX06 does not score higher than it does.

biggest_gap.what: The container's list rows and detail band are sized below their own content, and round 6 paid for the gold column out of the other columns' width rather than out of the row's. Measured: pitching the three columns against usable=144 units instead of half=198 cut every column 27%, which truncated 3 of 4 visible names and — unreported by the builder — the WEIGHT column, rendering 'Bog-iron maul 11.5' as 'Bog-iron ... 11...'. The net matter loss drops container D2 from 0.1538 to 0.1459, across RI-UIX09 DN4's 0.15 hard-fail floor. Separately the band shows 2 of the 4-6 wrapped lines that 42 of 45 carried records need, violating RI-UIX03 C7.
biggest_gap.why_it_matters: The player opens a chest and cannot read what a thing weighs or what it is called, on the one screen whose entire job is deciding what to carry and what to leave behind.

remedy.action: In game/src/ui/screens/inventory.js drawContainer(), stop making the three columns compete inside a 182-unit row: either give the container screen its own wider inner width (the panel is 480 of 1920 px and RI-UIX03 P5's ceiling is 60% of screen AREA, so there is room), or right-align the weight+gold pair against the row's right edge and give the name column the remainder. Reflow container.band so the description fits by layout rather than by ellipsis.
remedy.acceptance: All of: (1) ZERO weight values ellipsised across all seven rows on both sides at the shipped ui-journal fixture — a number is drawn whole or the column is widened until it is; (2) at most 1 item name ellipsised across both sides; (3) container.band renders >= 4 wrapped lines, satisfying RI-UIX03 C7 for the 42 of 45 carried records needing 4+, by reflow and not by shrinking type below RI-UIX06's readability floor; (4) PRESERVATION per S59 — container D2 >= 0.15 AND >= 0.1538 (its value at 76cd4848), and level-up D2 not below 0.1495 — every number measured on a git worktree checked out at the DELIVERED commit and run through THAT WORKTREE'S OWN tools/ui/t4-r2-measure.mjs, with the manifest's commit field asserted equal to the delivered SHA before any number is believed.

secondary_observations: The builder's citation 'T4-r5.md line 773' does not resolve — that file is 472 lines. The intended source is T4-r5.json:773. The substance is correct and independently verified.
IC1 fails: the in-combat commitment is not narrated on screen. Not this round's code.
TS5: a 40-frame held KEYBOARD direction moves 1 row where the equivalent held TOUCH drag moves 6. The missing axis repeat is a keyboard defect, not device-neutral.
MAP1 did not run — the browser closed before the map leg. Scored 0 fail-closed.

The builder's 'only two commits touched game/src since the pin' is wrong: `git log 76cd4848..b0a9f716 -- game/` returns five, and lighting-recipes.js and sky.js changed as landed commits rather than as a sibling's uncommitted drift.

An absolute --out passed to tools/ui/t4-* was silently nested under a duplicated repo root (path.join, not path.resolve) until b4e62e58 fixed 13 tools this session. A duplicated-root path escapes the .gitignore written for the real path, so debris under it gets committed while the identical file at its true path is correctly ignored. Worth a HAZARDS section alongside §17.

Importing tools/ui/t4-r2-critic-measure.mjs for its d2() RUNS it, and its default --out is a FILED round's artifact directory (T4-r2c). I tripped this once this session and the file was restored. The tool's own header warns of it; the durable fix is to split d2()/decodePNG() into a library that has no side effect on import.

corpus_defects_filed.what: D2 is defined as the fraction of a panel's pixels differing from THE PANEL'S OWN MODAL COLOUR by dE > 6. The reference is re-derived per capture, and a large pixel population sits at the boundary. Measured this round: the sheet panel's modal colour moved [42,55,43] -> [45,57,45] across two captures differing by 166 pixels (0.06% of the panel), and D2 moved 0.0108. Level-up: 66 pixels (0.03%), D2 moved 0.0026. On the container, 0.67% of the panel lies in the dE 5.5-6.5 band and a threshold sweep of 5.0-7.0 spans ~0.0157 of D2.
corpus_defects_filed.why_it_matters: DN4's 0.15 hard-fail floor is being applied to a quantity whose response to imperceptible input change is several times the margins it adjudicates. Round 5 passed the container by 0.0038. A measure that can move 0.0108 on a 0.06% image change cannot reliably pass or fail anything near its floor.

arbitration_questions.question: S58's corrected mechanism says D2 fell in round 4 because the DENOMINATOR fell when the panel shrank. notes: The most useful thing in this verdict is not the score. It is that a filed verdict's numbers were challenged, the challenge was itself testable, and the test found the challenge void while confirming the original. Round 5's critic measured correctly.

The builder deserves saying plainly: it reported its own uncertainty at length, refused to game the metric when gaming it was available, declined to grow the box for a reason that turns out to be right, re-derived a critic's claim instead of trusting it, and declined to edit an instrument mid-round. Every one of those calls was correct. The experiment it built to defend itself was the one thing it got wrong, and it got it wrong in the direction of exonerating its own change.

The general lesson, and it generalises past this round: FOUR ARMS AGREEING TO FOUR DECIMAL PLACES IS NOT CONVERGENT EVIDENCE — IT IS THE SIGNATURE OF FOUR RUNS OF THE SAME THING. A control that cannot possibly differ from its treatment will always agree with it. HAZARDS §11 says to freeze arms by construction; the missing half is to VERIFY THE FREEZE HELD, and here the verification was free because every manifest already carried the commit it actually ran.
